Maya: heads up - our edge sample (esm bundle) is dropping Authorization header in runtime, which causes client retries. CJS sample behaves normally. Anyone seen ts/emit or bundler quirks like this?
Jun: interesting. can you paste the minimal repro code + tsconfig and bundler config?
Maya: yup, small repro attached. tsconfig: module=ESNext, target=ES2022, preserveValueImports=false (default), esModuleInterop=true. bundler: esbuild, target=es2022, minify=true.
Maya: sample call: `redwoodClient.request('/v1/p', { auth: token, headers: { 'x-app': 'demo' } })` -> in dev (ts-node) headers ok, in built esm bundle `Authorization` shows up as undefined and the runtime issues a 401 -> sdk retries twice.
Priya: could be a value-level wrapper getting elided. I've seen overload-only signatures (generics/overloads) lead to helper emit differences, especially with `esModuleInterop` + `preserveValueImports` off. bundlers sometimes tree-shake tiny forwarding helpers.
Jun: do you have the emitted JS around the request helper? is the `options` object being defaulted/flattened away?
Maya: emitted snippet from the esm bundle: ```
export function sendRequest(url, opts){ opts = opts || {}; const headers = opts.headers || {}; // but opts.auth was in a type-only overload so never materialized
// later: headers.Authorization = opts.auth?.token || undefined;```
Maya: note `opts.auth` is undefined here, despite being present in source. in cjs build the same file shows `headers.Authorization = opts.auth.token` as expected.
Priya: yup. workaround we used: make the wrapper runtime-visible (avoid purely type-only overloads), or add `/* @__keep */` style inlining to convince bundler to keep the helper. alternatively set `preserveValueImports: true` in tsconfig so types-only imports don't remove runtime refs.
Jun: also check `moduleResolution` setting - `bundler` vs `node` can affect import emit. esbuild expects ESM value shapes. and minify can rename small vars that cause property access to break if helper gets collapsed.
Maya: tried preserveValueImports=true and minify=false -> esm bundle now preserves auth forwarding and tests pass.
Priya: for typings side: overloads that only differ by type parameters can be entirely erased and if the implementation signature differs in arity you get a different emitted helper that may drop arguments. recommend matching implementation signature exactly and avoid optional rest params used only in types.
Jun: should we add an onboarding note in the devex samples about this edge-case? and maybe a small SDK change: export a runtime-forwarding wrapper (non-type-only) to be robust across bundle modes.
Maya: yes. I'll open a tiny PR to samples with a short section "ESM bundling pitfalls: auth missing" and include the tsconfig/bundler toggles that work.
BuildBot: CI: edge-esm-auth-repro #7 failed on node 20 (repro bundle shows missing header) :warning:
Priya: also adding a unit test in sdk-infra: compile minimal TS with our d.ts shapes with tsc+esbuild and assert runtime options include auth. less flaky if we assert on emitted js rather than runtime behavior.
Jun: thanks, keep me posted. tagging infra for follow-up if SDK d.ts shape changes are needed. :pray:
